newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila to sell Meralco shares before end-97.
newsitem.headline: Manila to sell Meralco shares before end-97.

text.p: The Philippines' Presidential Commission on Good Government (PCGG) said on Wednesday its 51 million Manila Electric Co (Meralco) shares will be sold to institutional investors before yearend at a price higher than the prevailing market price.

PCGG Commissioner Herminio Mendoza told Reuters that Merrill Lynch and Co Inc has been tapped as the financial advisor for the sale of the shares last month after the Cabinet-level Committee on Privatisation approved the sale.
The PCGG is the custodian of all sequestered assets of the late dictator Ferdinand Marcos and his business associates.
Mendoza said of the 51 million shares held by PCGG, about 30 million are A shares and the rest are class B.
"We are just picking the right time but not right now. We want to sell to institutional investors or those with synergistic activities with Meralco," Mendoza said.
Meralco is the country's biggest power distributor serving most of the northern main island of Luzon.

"Definitely, the price will be higher than the market price," Mendoza said. At the present price of Meralco shares, he said the government will be able to raise six billion pesos from the sale of its shares.
Mendoza said he was informed that a number of foreign companies have expressed interest to buy the shares. He could not elaborate.
Meralco B shares were the most actively traded issue, gaining seven pesos, or 5.34 percent, to 138 pesos by late trade. Meralco A shares climbed one peso to 87.50 pesos.
